question: Is a bigger world a better one?
answer: Take a happy population. Adding people whose lives are worth living seems no worse. Repeat, trading a little quality for more numbers each time, and you arrive at an enormous population whose lives are barely worth living — rated better than the first. Forty years on, nobody has an agreed way out.
move: Every reasonable-looking rule about population leads somewhere nobody accepts.
source: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, 1984; the repugnant conclusion
